jobs.title: Assistant Professor of Statistics (Limited Term)
jobs.institution: Columbia University in the City of New York: Department of Statistics
jobs.description:
The Department of Statistics invites applications for four-year term positions at the rank of Assistant Professor of Statistics to begin July 1, 2027. The initial term of appointment is one academic year with the possibility of renewal for three additional years. A PhD in statistics or a related field is required by the date of appointment, as is a commitment to high quality research and teaching in statistics and/or probability. Candidates will be expected to sustain an active research and publication agenda and to teach in the departmental undergraduate and graduate programs. Candidates with expertise in machine learning, big data, mathematical finance and probability theory are particularly encouraged to apply.
The department expects to support successful candidates with a generous research allowance. The expected teaching load is three semester-long courses per year.
The department currently consists of 36 faculty members and 60 PhD students. The department has been expanding rapidly and, like the University itself, is an extraordinarily vibrant academic community. We are especially interested in candidates who, through their research, teaching and/or service will contribute to the excellence of the academic community. For further information about the department and our activities, centers, research areas, and curricular programs, please go to our web page at: http://www.stat.columbia.edu
Review of applications will begin on December 1, 2026 and will continue until the positions are filled.

jobs.title: Faculty Fellow in Museum Studies (2 positions)
jobs.description:
NEW YORK UNIVERSITY
Faculty Fellow in Museum Studies
Program in Museum Studies
Arts & Science
The Program in Museum Studies, an interdisciplinary program in Arts & Science at New York University, invites applications for two (2) Faculty Fellow positions.
The initial appointment will be for one year beginning September 1, 2027, with the expectation of annual renewal for up to two additional years pending administrative and budgetary approval and satisfactory performance.
We seek committed scholars whose research interests engage with ethical and critical frameworks in museums, specifically in decolonial theory. The candidate should have demonstrated experience with student mentorship in academic and professional contexts. Their research should engage with diverse methodologies in museum studies, such as archival work, community engagement, cataloging, database management, and primary, source-based research.
Only candidates with professional experience in a museum or comparable cultural institution, such as archives, libraries, cultural centers, and heritage sites, will be considered.
Description:
As a faculty fellow, you will teach three courses (two in the fall semester and one in the spring) that include a required History and Theory of Museums course for first-year students and a graduate seminar related to your research offered as an elective in the spring semester. Additionally, you will work with the M.A. students to advise master's theses and actively participate in the life of a dynamic program.
Review of applications will begin on January 15, 2027, and continue until the search is complete.
NYU Program in Museum Studies
Museum Studies program offers a unique interdisciplinary academic foundation in museum history and practice. Consisting of coursework, research, and a required internship, the MA program provides a well-rounded look at museums with the ability to center a focus on a particular discipline in art, history, science, anthropology, or any other field. The program's knowledgeable faculty and adjunct faculty and its international network of dedicated alumni help students expand their careers and experiences both inside and outside of the classroom.
Core classes are designed for students to understand the historical and theoretical implications of current museum practice, development and management of collections and exhibitions, and a comprehensive account of the administrative, strategic, and financial aspects of museum management. In addition to our core courses, students choose from a wide range of electives that further and deepen their understanding of museum practice and engagement. The program attracts a diverse student body, including students from all over the world. Inclusive classroom experiences are essential for our teaching.
Arts & Science at NYU is at the heart of a leading research university that spans the globe. We seek scholars of the highest caliber who are sensitive to the needs of and possess an interest in working in a broad academic community with different viewpoints and backgrounds. NYU affirms the value of differing perspectives on the world as we strive to build the strongest possible university with the widest reach. To learn more about the Arts & Sciences commitment to inclusive excellence, please read here: https://as.nyu.edu/departments/facultyexcellence.html.
In compliance with NYC’s Pay Transparency Act, the annual base salary for this position is $60,000. New York University considers factors such as (but not limited to) the scope and responsibilities of the position, the candidate’s work experience, education/training, key skills, internal peer equity, as well as market and organizational considerations when extending an offer.

jobs.title: Associate Professor - Neuromuscular Medicine Neurologist – CE Track
jobs.institution: University of Pennsylvania: Perelman School of Medicine - Neurology
jobs.description:
The Department of Neurology at the Perelman School of Medicine at the University of Pennsylvania seeks candidates for an Associate Professor position in the non-tenure clinician educator track. Expertise is required in the specific area of Neuromuscular Ultrasound and/or Autonomic expertise. Applicants must have an M.D. degree. Board certified in Neurology and Neuromuscular Medicine is required.
Teaching responsibilities may include teaching neuromuscular fellows, residents, and medical students during their rotations in the EMG lab, outpatient clinic, and inpatient services. The NM faculty will also provide lectures on topics pertinent to neuromuscular diseases and the Department of Neurology throughout the year.
Clinical responsibilities may include the NM faculty seeing neuromuscular patients in the outpatient clinic and perform EMGs; Special interest in CMT is encouraged.
Research or scholarship responsibilities may include the NM faculty participating in ongoing clinic trials in the division as an investigator.
Applicants who are mid-career are encouraged to apply.

jobs.title: Assistant Professor Academic Clinician – Neurohospitalist
jobs.institution: University of Pennsylvania: Perelman School of Medicine - Neurology
jobs.description:
The Department of Neurology at the Perelman School of Medicine at the University of Pennsylvania seeks candidates for an Assistant Professor position in the non-tenure academic clinician track. Expertise is required in the specific area of of quality improvement/clinical effectiveness, medical education and clinical care. The department is seeking applicants who are highly experienced in inpatient neurology. Applicants must have an M.D or M.D./Ph.D. degree. The successful candidate must be board eligible in Neurology.
Teaching responsibilities may include teaching medical students and residents on bedside rounds for the consult and inpatient services. Subspecialty interests are also encouraged.
Clinical responsibilities may include attending on the inpatient neurology services at Virtua-Our Lady of Lourdes via the Penn-Virtua Alliance and at one or more of our downtown Philadelphia hospitals to complement the growing group of Neurohospitalists.

jobs.title: Professor of Digital Systems, AI and Business* (f/m/d)
jobs.institution: WHU Otto Beisheim School of Management
jobs.description:
We seek a scholar who investigates how digital technologies and artificial intelligence transform business and management. The ideal candidate combines a deep understanding of technological possibilities with rigorous research into their economic, organizational, and managerial implications. We particularly welcome research that examines the workings of intelligent digital systems, what they enable, and how they transform decision-making, organizational processes, and business models. Relevant topics may include AI-supported decision systems, intelligent automation, digital platforms and business models, customer interaction, and their effects on market or firm outcomes. We value the ability to design and develop innovative digital or AI-enabled systems and tools. The successful candidate will bring a technology-informed perspective to teaching and engage with both technological innovators and managerial audiences.
The professorship will strengthen WHU's research, teaching, and industry collaboration at the intersection of digital technologies, AI, and business. *The precise title and group affiliation will reflect the selected candidate's profile.

jobs.title: Professor of Digital Systems, AI and Production (f/m/d)
jobs.institution: WHU Otto Beisheim School of Management: Supply Chain Management Group
jobs.description:
We seek a scholar who investigates how digital technologies and artificial intelligence transform the design, management, and performance of production and supply chains. The ideal candidate combines a deep understanding of technological possibilities with rigorous research into their economic, organizational, and operational implications.
We particularly welcome research that engages with how intelligent digital systems work, what they make possible, and how they transform planning, coordination, and decision-making. Relevant topics may include AI-supported decision systems, intelligent automation, robotics, human–AI collaboration, or digitally enabled business models. The successful candidate will bring a technology-informed perspective to teaching and engage with both technological innovators and managerial audiences.
The professorship is based in WHU’s Supply Chain Management Group and will strengthen its research, teaching, and industry collaboration at the intersection of digital technologies, production, and supply chains.

jobs.title: Research: Research Assistant Professor
jobs.description:
The Department of Pharmacy Practice of the Irma Lerma Rangel College of Pharmacy at Texas A&M University invites applications for a full-time, research-track position (non-tenured) with an 11-month academic appointment beginning December 1, 2026. Applicants will be considered for the faculty title of Research Assistant Professor.
The position requires research, service, and teaching to the Department/College, the profession, and the public. The position provides opportunities for an individual with a strong commitment to an academic career emphasizing innovative research, service, teaching, and scholarly activities. Research activity and teaching activity are required; publication and presentation activity, as well as professional and college services are expected. Academic responsibilities include teaching topics related to pharmacy law, practice, skills classes, and health education to students and residents, as assigned. Traveling between the campuses of the Rangel College of Pharmacy is expected and common.
The recruited individual will be integral in assisting and guiding the research for the Department of Pharmacy Practice Laboratory and undertaking research that translates or impacts clinical pharmacy practice related field. In addition, the selected individuals will be responsible for establishing or overseeing the development of new analytical, molecular biology and related techniques and developing new research areas for extramural funding. The applicants should be well versed in clinical pharmacy, drug development, and in vitro and/or in vivo models and be able to write reports for the assigned projects.
The selected candidate will also engage in writing grant applications, manuscripts for publications, and contributing to ongoing projects. and communicating research results at scientific meetings. Additionally, the selected candidates will assist in teaching and mentoring graduate students and overseeing laboratory staff engaged in research projects.

jobs.title: Practice-Track Faculty Position (Goizueta IMPACT)
jobs.description:
Emory University's Goizueta Business School invites applications for a full-time, open-rank practice-track faculty position to teach in the Goizueta IMPACT curriculum, beginning in Fall 2027. We seek a seasoned business practitioner with extensive corporate experience in problem solving, strategy, client relationship management, and project leadership. Candidates with deep experience applying the structured problem-solving toolkit used by top-tier management consulting firms are preferred.
This is an open-rank search across three faculty areas: Organization & Management (O&M), Marketing, and Information Systems & Operations Management (ISOM). The successful candidate's faculty appointment will be housed in the area that most closely aligns with their professional background, expertise, and functional experience.
The standard teaching load is six full-semester courses per academic year. In addition, the faculty member will support Goizueta IMPACT program leadership across multiple degree programs, helping students apply structured problem-solving methods to real client engagements. The primary responsibilities for this position include teaching, service to the school and university, support of Goizueta IMPACT programming, and other related responsibilities as assigned.
Goizueta has a vibrant practice track where colleagues are respected and valued for their contributions to teaching and service. Service to the Goizueta community is expected, consistent with expectations for our full-time faculty. Goizueta Business School's undergraduate BBA is ranked No. 14 nationally by U.S. News (2025) and No. 8 by Poets & Quants (2025); its full-time MBA is ranked No. 17 by U.S. News (2025) and No. 23 by Poets & Quants (2024–2025). Emory University is located in Atlanta, Georgia, one of the best cities in the United States to work in and a significant hub for both domestic and international travel. Home to a substantial concentration of Fortune 500 companies, Atlanta offers numerous opportunities to collaborate closely with industry leaders and prominent healthcare institutions.
The initial term of employment is three years, with contract renewal contingent upon satisfactory performance.
About Goizueta IMPACT
Goizueta IMPACT is the school's signature approach to experiential learning across its MBA graduate programs, built to bridge theory and practice. Students learn how to apply a structured problem-solving process to real-world problems. The course content includes problem solving, influential communication, and managing internal and external stakeholders. As a degree requirement, graduate student teams solve a strategically important challenge for a sponsoring organization.
Teams are supported by faculty advisors, second-year IMPACT Coaching Fellows, and external coaches, and present their recommendations at the IMPACT Showcase, judged by more than 300 external business leaders. IMPACT runs across Goizueta's One-Year and Two-Year full-time MBA, Executive and Evening Working Professional MBA, and Master of Business for Veterans (MBV) programs, preparing students to deliver results from day one of their internships and careers.
Learn more at https://goizueta.emory.edu/corporate/consult/mba.

jobs.title: First-Year Engineering - Sessional Assistant Professor, Teaching Stream
jobs.institution: York University - Lassonde School of Engineering: Electrical Engineering & Computer Science
jobs.description:
The Department of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science in the Lassonde School of Engineering at York University invites highly qualified applicants for a Sessional Assistant Professor, Teaching Stream position in First-Year Engineering. This is an open Contractually Limited Appointment (CLA) to the teaching stream for a three-year term commencing July 1, 2027.
Our first-year engineering program provides an engaging and supportive learning experience that connects mathematics, science, computing, and design to authentic engineering challenges from day one. Students learn in technology-enabled active learning classrooms and have access to a dedicated makerspace that supports hands-on design, prototyping, and innovation. With small learning communities, project-based experiences, and close interaction with faculty, the program offers an exceptional foundation for success in engineering and beyond.
The successful candidate will contribute to first-year engineering education through the teaching of engineering communication, ethics, engineering design, and introductory programming, including the development of software applications that interact with sensors and physical systems. The appointee may also serve as Coordinator, First-Year Engineering at the Markham Campus and will provide educational leadership supporting the growth of engineering programming and the campus. Responsibilities may include curriculum development and coordination, team teaching, pedagogical innovation, and the integration of professional skills and project-based learning across the first-year experience.
The successful applicant will join the faculty members based at York’s new Markham Campus. York University’s Markham Campus offers state-of-the-art facilities to provide innovative job-ready academic programming and research focusing on core themes of technology and entrepreneurship as applied in different contexts, disciplines and professional fields. Building on York University’s academic presence in the City of Markham, the new campus will help fulfil future labour market and civic leadership needs by providing transferable 21st century skills that are at the core of future economic competitiveness and community development in Markham, York Region and across Ontario. Collaboration with York University’s existing research strengths in the core areas of the new campus and dynamic engagement with the area’s businesses, industries, and communities will create an innovative, cross-disciplinary, and social justice-oriented research culture for solving complex problems that transcend traditional disciplines.
Hiring Policies:
The anticipated starting salary for this position at the rank of Sessional Assistant Professor is in the range of $125,000 to $155,000 and will be commensurate with qualifications and experience. York University offers generous benefits and salary provisions.
All York University positions are subject to budgetary approval.
York is an Affirmative Action (AA) employer and strongly values diversity, including gender and sexual diversity, in its community. Details of the AA Program, which applies to women, members of racialized groups, Indigenous peoples, persons with disabilities and those who identify as 2SLGBTQ+, can be found here or by contacting Aqsa Ahmed, EDI Program Manager (aqsa517@yorku.ca).
York welcomes and employs scholars from all over the world. All qualified candidates are encouraged to apply; however, Canadian citizens and permanent residents will be given priority.
York has a policy on Accommodation in Employment for Persons with Disabilities and is committed to working towards a barrier-free workplace and expanding the accessibility of the workplace to persons with disabilities. Applicants who require accommodation are invited to contact Kleanthi Markakis, Administrative Assistant, at mkmasap@yorku.ca.
The use of artificial intelligence will be used to screen, assess, or select applicants. Applicants who require more information are invited to contact Kleanthi Markakis, Administrative Assistant, mkmasap@yorku.ca.
Learn More About York:
York University generates and shares knowledge through our research, teaching and engagement with communities around the world. The 2023-2028 Strategic Research Plan showcases the depth, breadth and ambition of research at York.
York’s commitments to social justice are laid out in our Decolonizing, Equity, Diversity and Inclusion Strategy, the Framework & Action Plan on Black Inclusion and the Indigenous Framework for York University.
Follow the activities and accomplishments of York’s faculty, students and staff on YFile.

jobs.title: Assistant or Associate Professor of Pathology, Hematopathology
jobs.institution: Howard University College of Medicine: Pathology
jobs.description:
The Department of Pathology at Howard University College of Medicine invites applications for a full-time faculty position at the Assistant or Associate Professor level, on the tenure track or clinician-educator track. We seek a hematopathologist to provide diagnostic services in hematologic disease, sign out surgical pathology cases, serve as Medical Director of the Hematopathology Section, and teach pathology to medical students, residents, and fellows. The role works closely with Howard's hematology and oncology programs and its long-established sickle cell disease program.
Candidates with interests in molecular hematopathology, hemoglobinopathies, lymphoma and leukemia classification, or laboratory quality and informatics are especially encouraged to apply.
Primary Responsibilities
Clinical Care
Interpret peripheral blood smears, bone marrow aspirates and biopsies, lymph node and extranodal specimens, and flow cytometry. Perform surgical pathology case sign-out.
Integrate cytogenetic, FISH, and molecular findings into comprehensive hematopathology reports.
Serve as Medical Director of the Hematopathology Section.
Provide oversight of hematology, coagulation, flow cytometry, or hemoglobin analysis laboratories, including quality assurance and CAP and CLIA compliance.
Participate in tumor boards and clinical consultation with hematology and oncology colleagues.
Teaching and Education
Teach pathology and hematology content in the pre-clerkship curriculum through lectures, laboratories, and small-group instruction.
Teach, train, and supervise pathology residents and rotating trainees in hematopathology and surgical pathology at the sign-out bench and in conferences.
Advise and mentor medical students and trainees in clinical and scholarly work.
Research and Scholarship
Pursue scholarship in hematologic disease, including hemoglobinopathies and hematologic malignancies.
Publish peer-reviewed scholarship and collaborate on clinical and translational studies.
Academic Service
Serve on department, hospital, College, and University committees.
Contribute to the clinical, educational, research, and service missions of Howard University.

jobs.title: Assistant or Associate Professor: Tenure Track
jobs.description:
The Department of Epidemiology at the Geisel School of Medicine at Dartmouth and the Molecular Epidemiology Center for Biomedical Research Excellence invites applications for a tenure track faculty position at the Assistant or Associate level. We seek candidates with a strong track record of leading innovative, independent research programs in molecular epidemiology over the lifecourse. Priority areas include experience in the design and conduct of large-scale prospective molecular epidemiologic investigations, studies with global impact focusing on the environment and planetary health, use of geospatial methods, and addressing rural populations. Outstanding candidates working in other areas of molecular epidemiology are also encouraged to apply. The department further has emerging strength in Implementation Sciences and is also interested in applicants with independent research programs in implementation research using molecular epidemiology. The Department offers a dynamic, interdisciplinary, and highly collaborative setting with a commitment and infrastructure to support rigorous and impactful research and career advancement.
Dartmouth faculty benefit from close collaborative relationships with other departments across the medical school, university, and medical center, including with the College of Arts & Sciences, Thayer School of Engineering, and Tuck School of Business. In addition, Dartmouth is home to an NCI Designated Comprehensive Cancer Center with four research programs, including Cancer Population Sciences, and the Dartmouth Center for Implementation Science. As a part of success in this role, there are expectations for teaching and mentoring. Individuals will have opportunities to participate in multiple graduate programs (e.g., the Program in Quantitative Biomedical Sciences, Implementation Science, Integrative Neuroscience, the Dartmouth Institute for Health Policy and Clinical Practice, and the Program in Molecular and Cellular Biology).
Dartmouth is committed to academic excellence and encourages the open exchange of ideas within a culture of mutual respect. Dartmouth welcomes people with different backgrounds, life experiences, and perspectives and believes that diversity in all its forms enhances academic excellence. Applicants should address in their cover letter how their research, teaching, service, and/or life experiences prepare them to serve Dartmouth’s commitment to academic excellence in an environment that is welcoming to all.

jobs.title: Assistant Professor of Analytical Chemistry
jobs.description:
The Department of Natural Sciences in the College of Arts, Sciences, and Letters (CASL) invites applications for a tenure-track Assistant Professor of Analytical Chemistry, with a preferred starting date of August 30, 2027. We seek a colleague who will develop a productive, externally funded research program, provide excellent teaching, and mentor undergraduate students.
Our multidisciplinary department offers programs in chemistry, biochemistry, biological sciences, environmental science, physics, and related fields. As an R2 research institution, UM-Dearborn values the scholar-teacher model, research-informed education, and undergraduate research experiences. The successful candidate will play an important role in strengthening the Analytical Chemistry and Instrumental Analysis area, including laboratory and instrumentation-based education, while supporting the continued development of its American Chemical Society (ACS)-approved chemistry program.
Research specialties within analytical chemistry are open, and may include spectroscopy, electrochemistry, separations, mass spectrometry, chemical sensing, bioanalytical or environmental chemistry, materials characterization, and emerging data-intensive methods. The successful candidate will be expected to seek external funding, publish peer-reviewed articles, present research at national conferences, and mentor students in research. The University highly values research involving both undergraduate and graduate students. Laboratory facilities and competitive start-up funding will be provided, and interdisciplinary collaboration is strongly encouraged.
The teaching load is 2:2 (two courses per semester), with opportunities to teach general chemistry, analytical chemistry, instrumental analysis, associated laboratories courses, and other undergraduate or graduate courses aligned with the candidate's expertise and departmental needs. Faculty are also expected to contribute to departmental, university, and professional service and to foster an inclusive, collegial, and collaborative academic environment.
This is an on-site position and expected to teach in various modalities.
Campus and Community Information
The University of Michigan-Dearborn was founded in 1959 on 200 acres of the original Henry Ford Estate in Dearborn, Michigan. As one of the University of Michigan's three campuses, we serve over 8,000 students and provide high-quality undergraduate, graduate, professional, and continuing education programs that embody the prestige of the University of Michigan name. Our mission is rooted in a commitment to Metro Detroit's well-being and diversity, fostering a caring, dynamic, intellectual, and socially welcoming environment.
UM-Dearborn utilizes the Boyer Model of academic scholarship. We distinguish ourselves by building and nurturing intentional, mutually beneficial partnerships with local industries, governments, and community organizations. Our faculty are recognized for their excellence in scholarship and teaching and are actively engaged in professional and academic service. UM-Dearborn offers ample opportunities for creative, collaborative research, practice-based learning, and community engagement through scholarly and educational partnerships. Faculty have the privilege of working closely with their students, 47% of whom are first-generation college students, 46% are Pell Grant-eligible, and 31% are students of color.
The average class size is 25 students, and 69% of classes have fewer than 30 students. U.S. News & World Report consistently ranks UM-Dearborn among the best regional universities in the Midwest. In 2024, UM-Dearborn ranked the number-one regional public university in Michigan and third in the Midwest. The university is also recognized on Forbes' list of America's Top Colleges. For more information, please visit our website at www.umdearborn.edu.
Dearborn is a vibrant, diverse community centrally located within one of America’s largest business regions. The area provides a variety of urban, suburban, and rural environments within a reasonable commute, including Detroit, its suburbs, and Ann Arbor.

jobs.title: Assistant Professor in Medicinal Chemistry or Pharmacology
jobs.description:

We seek an experimental scientist with a strong record of scholarly productivity and a demonstrated commitment to mentoring undergraduate and graduate students, particularly those pursuing pre-health and biomedical sciences. The preferred starting date is August 30, 2027.
The Department of Natural Sciences is a collaborative community serving more than 600 majors in Chemistry, Biochemistry, and Biological Sciences, with a strong focus on pre-health and biomedical sciences. We value high-impact, research-informed teaching and meaningful research experiences for a diverse student body, including first-generation and Pell-eligible students. Opportunities for interdisciplinary collaboration exist, including with programs in bioengineering.

The department encourages interdisciplinary research collaboration and student mentorship.
The teaching load is 2:2 (two courses per semester), including organic chemistry and graduate-level courses such as Biochemical Pharmacology.
